title: Salters Cottages

description.main: An artist's book of stills from Salters Cottages, a sixteen-minute 16mm film Gary Schneider made in 1981 at a summer cottage colony on Long Island, with Peter Hujar, John Erdman, Suzanne Joelson and Gary Stephan as its cast. An homage to Jean Genet's Un Chant d'Amour, the film is dedicated to Hujar. Dashwood Books published the book in 2019 in a first edition of 1,000 copies, printed in quadtone.
description.extended:
An artist's book of stills from Salters Cottages, the sixteen-minute 16mm film Gary Schneider shot in 1981 at a summer cottage colony on Long Island, with Peter Hujar among its cast. Dashwood Books published it in 2019; Schneider dedicated it to Hujar, his friend and mentor.

The film's only sound is a Bell and Howell projector. It follows the voyeuristic and exhibitionist habits of the colony's residents, played by Hujar, John Erdman, Suzanne Joelson and Gary Stephan as the watchers and the watched, and Schneider made it as an homage to Jean Genet's Un Chant d'Amour (1950). Jerry Kelly and Schneider designed the book; Wilco Art Books printed the black-and-white frames in quadtone. Softcover, 124 pages, first edition of 1,000 copies. It was launched at the Jeu de Paume in Paris during the museum's Hujar exhibition, where the film was also screened.

Schneider (b. 1954, East London, South Africa) came to New York in the late 1970s from painting, performance and film. In 1981 he and Erdman, his partner, founded the printing studio Schneider/Erdman, where he printed for Hujar before his own long-exposure portraits and the Genetic Self-Portrait (1997–98) made his name. The library also holds Gary Schneider: Portraits (Yale, 2004) and his memoir Peter Hujar: Behind the Camera and in the Darkroom (2024).
description.artist_bio: Gary Schneider was born 25 November 1954 in East London, South Africa, and lives and works in New York. BFA Michaelis School of Fine Art, Cape Town; MFA Pratt Institute. With his partner John Erdman he founded the printing studio Schneider/Erdman Inc. in 1981 and became a master printer for other photographers, including Peter Hujar. Known for long-exposure portraits and the Genetic Self-Portrait (1997-98). Work in the Whitney, Guggenheim, Art Institute of Chicago, Harvard Art Museums, MFA Boston, National Gallery of Canada; Guggenheim Fellowship, NEA grant, Lou Stoumen Award, Eisenstaedt Award.
description.exhibition_context: The book was launched at the Jeu de Paume, Paris, during the museum's Peter Hujar exhibition in autumn 2019, where the film was also screened (per the printer Wilco Art Books / Colour & Books).
